Elba::11.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: Check dive. After breakfast, a welcome briefing will be presented by the guide. A check of your diving documents and insurance will be conducted. The captain will then set course for the first dive site, approximately 30 minutes from departure. The 'reorientation' dive briefing will be given by the guide. The second dive will take place in the afternoon. Depending on your departure marina and weather conditions, this program may be subject to change. Day 3: On this day, three dives will be offered at the Daedalus site, a potential meeting place with hammerhead sharks. Day 4: You will undertake three dives around the Rocky and Zabargad Islands. The navigation times between the sites vary from 30 to 45 minutes between the islands. The dive sites are carefully selected by your guide based on the weather and the number of boats at the sites. Day 5: For the first day on Elba, you will arrive at the Shaab Kabrit reef to conduct two dives on the Isola Di Levanzo wreck. A third dive will be carried out on the reef. Day 6: Continuing within the Elba Nature Reserve, the captain will take you to Gota Kabrit. After a 1-hour and 30-minute journey, a second dive will be conducted at the Habili Shalal site. Finally, a last dive will be offered at the Ohrob site, a 2- hour and 30-minute navigation away. This program is subject to change based on weather conditions. Day 7: After spending two days on the Elba Reef, you will head north to the Abu Fendira area, near Saint John's. Three dives will be carried out at Abu Fendira. Day 8: In the early morning, the captain and his crew will take you to the Saint John's sites. Three dives will be offered. Navigation times between the sites vary between 30 minutes and 1 hour and 30 minutes in the Saint John's area. Dive sites are carefully selected by your guide based on the weather and the number of boats at the sites. Day 9: We continue our journey northward. On the way, we will stop at Sataya, located in the Fury Shoals area, where you may have the opportunity to swim with dolphins. Three dives will be conducted in the area. Day 10: In the early morning, you will arrive in the Marsa Alam area, at the legendary Elphinstone Reef. You will do 2 dives there before sailing for another two hours to arrive at the Port Ghalib marina in the early afternoon. You can use the rear platform to rinse your equipment. Your guide will also offer various non-diving activities to keep you occupied on Friday afternoon. Day 11: In the morning, you will undertake two dives in the Port Ghalib area, including a search for the green turtles of Shouna. Return to the marina, and you will have the option to stay overnight on the boat on Tuesday evening. Day 12: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Fury Shoals & Dolphins::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, your guide will tell you everything you need to know about your program of the week, safety recommendations, and, more generally, your life on the boat. Your diving certifications, logbook and insurance will be checked for certified divers before leaving the marina. The captain will make his way to the first snorkeling site. It will also be possible to dive on this site for certified divers. The briefing of the so-called "check dive" will be presented to you by the guide. After lunch, you will sail south to the second snorkeling / diving site of the day. Before dinner, for those who wish, you can attend a presentation on the fauna and flora of the Red Sea. In the early evening, after dinner, the boat will continue south to reach the Sataya area overnight. Day 3: In the morning the guide will tell you everything you need to know on “how to behave in the company of dolphins” for a respectful encounter with them. A first snorkeling trip with the dolphins will be organized. For certified divers who wish, a dive can be offered to you, outside the Sataya lagoon, where diving is prohibited. You are not certified divers and you want to discover the underwater world in scuba diving ? Your guide can offer you an introduction to scuba diving. All you need to do is notify them early enough in the day so that they can adapt their program accordingly. Your guide will suggest several activities throughout the day. Diving, snorkeling along the reef, swimming, snorkeling with dolphins ... the choice is yours. At night, a splendid starry landscape will occupy your evening after dinner. Day 4: After having enjoyed another moment of bliss with the dolphins in the morning, the captain and his crew will move the boat to one of the most beautiful sites of the Fury Shoals. You will go on a snorkeling trip along the reef to observe the incredible biodiversity of the Red Sea. For certified divers, you will have the opportunity to immerse yourself in a magnificent coral garden. Depending on your wishes, a second dive can be organized in the afternoon on another Fury Shoals site, or a second excursion with the dolphins inside the lagoon of Sataya. Did you take photos during the day ? A large screen awaits you in the lounge to present your photos to the whole group, your guide will be happy to comment on them after dinner. Day 5: Feel free to choose what you want to do : swim with dolphins, immerse yourself in one of the Fury Shoals sites, take a snorkeling hike along a reef and observe the magnificent colors of the Red Sea, make an intro dive... Your guide will adapt the program according to your wishes. Day 6: After breakfast, a dolphin excursion and a dive for certified divers will be organized. You will then sail approximately 5 to 6 hours north to reach the site of Sheleneyat. You can take a snorkeling hike along the reef. After dinner, time to party ! Day 7: At the break of dawn, the boat will sail to the Marsa Alam area where you will go diving or snorkeling on the two sites selected by your guide. You will arrive at the marina early in the afternoon. Your guide will tell you all about the leisure activities you can book in the Marsa Alam area to spend an entertaining Friday afternoon. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Golden Triangle / BDE::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, your guide will tell you everything you need to know about your programme of the week, safety recommendations and, more generally, your life on the boat. Your diving certifications, logbook, and insurance will be checked before leaving the marina. The boat will then sail to the first dive site, 30 minutes away from the marina. Your guide will give you a detailed briefing about your first dive. The second dive will be done in the afternoon. After dinner, the boat will head towards the Brothers Islands for a six hour long trip. This program may be subject to change according to weather conditions and the marina you will depart from. Day 3: Arrived the day before on site, you will do three daytime dives on the stunning drop-offs of the Brothers Islands. Due to new regulations aimed at protecting the marine ecosystem, safari boats are only allowed to spend one day on the Brothers' site. You will then sail all night long to reach Daedalus at the break of dawn. Day 4: Arrived early in the morning, you will do three daytime dives on the amazing drop-off of Daedalus, home of the hammerhead shark. A visit to the lighthouse will be organised by the guide with the authorisation of the keepers. Day 5: According to the weather forecast and customers' requests, you will do two or three more dives on Daedalus before sailing towards the coast. It will take about seven hours to reach the site of Abu Dabbab where you will spend the night. According to your time of arrival, a night dive may be organized. Day 6: According to the weather forecast, you will do two or three dives on the stunning drop-offs of Elphinstone. Then the boat will sail back to Abu Dabbab to spend the night in a protected area. If a night dive has not been organized the day before, then we will organize it this day. Day 7: According to the weather forecast and your flight schedules, you will do one or two more dives in the morning. After the last dive, you will have the possibility to rinse all your diving gear on the diving deck at the rear of the boat before sailing for 2 hours to Port Ghalib. This program is based on a departure from Port Ghalib, it can be modified without prior notice by the captain and/or the guide according to the weather conditions. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure, or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

North - Brother Islands::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, your guide will tell you everything you need to know about your programme of the week, safety recommendations and, more generally, your life on the boat. Your diving certifications, logbook and insurance will be checked before leaving the marina. The boat will then sail to the first dive site, 30 minutes away from the marina. Your guide will give you a detailed briefing about your first dive. After lunch you will do your second dive. You will then keep sailing north to reach the El Gouna area where you will spend a quiet and peaceful night moored behind a big reef. Day 3: Arrived the day before on site, you will do your first-two wreck dives in the morning. After lunch you will sail north for two hours before reaching the site where you will do the third dive of the day. Upon request, a night dive may be added. For a quiet and pea ceful night, you will spend the night awa y from the waves, moored behind a bi g reef. This programme may be subject t o change according to weather conditio ns. Day 4: Discover the fascinating history of this World War II cargo ship, now an underwater museum teeming with marine life. Explore its holds filled with trucks, motorcycles, and war supplies, all encrusted in corals. Each dive reveals new secrets, making it a truly unforgettable experience for every diver. Day 5: At the break of dawn, the boat will sail to the Ras Muhammad marine park where you will dive twice on the dizzying drop-offs among thousands of colourful fishes. After lunch, the boat will start heading south. The third dive will either be done on a beautiful coral garden or on a shipwreck. Upon request (and according to the site and weather), a n ight dive may be added. Day 6: Arrived in the early morning, you will make three dives during the day on the magnificent drop offs of the Brothers. A tour of the lighthouse can be organized by your guide according to agreements with the guards on site. The captain and his crew will then sail for around five hours to arrive at night in the Safaga a rea. Day 7: The last two dives of the week will be in Hurghada or Safaga, with beautiful drop-offs. After diving, gear can be rinsed on the boat before heading to the marina. Arrival is around 2:00 PM, and leisure activities can be arranged for the afternoon. St John's Reef::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, your guide will tell you everything you need to know about your program of the week, safety recommendations, and, more generally, your life on the boat. Your diving certifications, logbook and insurance will be checked before leaving the marina. The boat will then sail to the first dive site, 30 minutes away from the marina. Your guide will give you a detailed briefing about your first dive. After lunch, you will sail for about two hours heading south to reach the dive site called “Gota Sharm” where you will do your second dive. After dinner, the boat will sail all night long, crossing the Tropic of Cancer on its way, to reach the Saint John's reef area at the break of dawn. Day 3: Saint John's Reef : 3 dives will be organized. The sailing time between the dive sites varies from 30 min to 1h30. The dive sites are carefully selected by your guide according to the weather forecast and the number of boats already moored on the site. For a quiet and peaceful night, you will spend the night moored behind a big reef. Day 4: At sunrise, the captain and his crew will take you to another fantastic dive site of Saint John's reef for another great day of diving. Day 5: One last dive on Saint John's before sailing up north. Halfway between the Saint John's area and the Fury Shoals, we will stop for a mythical dive: the caves of Um Kararim. Then we will reach Sataya (Dolphin House) in the Fury Shoals area. According to your time of arrival and the light, you will have the opportunity to go snorkeling with dolphins. The third dive of the day will either take place at dusk or at night. The boat will be moored on Sataya reef for the night. Day 6: If the snorkeling session with the dolphins has not been organized the day before, we will organize it this morning. Then we will go diving on two beautiful reefs of the Fury Shoals area. After lunch, the boat will head north for a 5 hour sail to reach the site called “Sheleneyat”. The third dive of the day will either take place at dusk or at night according to your time of arrival. After dinner, the captain and his crew will organize a surprise Egyptian event. Day 7: The boat will sail for 45 min before you reach your first dive site of the day. After breakfast, you will sail north for two hours to reach the Marsa Alam area where you will do your last dive. After the dive, you will have the possibility to rinse all your diving gear on the diving deck at the rear of the boat before sailing for 30 min to the marina. The estimated time of arrival is 2:00 PM (your guide will tell you all about the leisure activities you can book in the Marsa Alam area to spend an entertaining Friday afternoon). Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. The Mixed South::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, a welcome briefing (organization of the week, safety instructions on board...) will be presented to you by the guide. Your diving documents and insurance will be checked before leaving the marina. The captain will sail to the first dive site 30 minutes from departure. The briefing of the check-dive dive will be presented to you by the guide. The second dive will be done during the afternoon. In the early evening, after dinner, the boat will start its journey towards Daedalus. About 7 hours of navigation will be required. Depending on the weather this program can be modified. Day 3: At sunrise, you will start your day of diving on the Daedalus falls. Your guide will suggest three dives. This reef offers you ten different dives. You will make 2 dives north of the reef for perhaps the chance to observe hammerhead sharks. In the afternoon, you will dive west of the reef where the coral diversity is impressive. This slope also offers perfect light in the afternoon. Between dives, you will have the opportunity to visit the Daedalus lighthouse. In the early evening, after dinner, the boat will continue its journey all night south to arrive in the early morning under the Tropic of Cancer at Rocky Island and Zabargad. Day 4: You will make three dives around the Rocky and Zabargad islands. The navigation times between the sites vary from 30 to 45 minutes between the islands. The dive sites are carefully chosen by your guide depending on the weather and the number of boats on the sites. Day 5: In the early morning, the captain and his crew will take you to the Saint John's sites. Three dives will be offered to you. Navigation times between sites vary between 30 minutes and 1 hour 30 minutes in the Saint John's area. The dive sites are carefully chosen by your guide depending on the weather and the number of boats on the sites. Day 6: That day, we will start the ascent to the north. On the way, we will stop at Sataya (Dolphin house) located in the Fury Shoals area, where you may have the opportunity to swim with the dolphins. We will then continue our ascent to the Sheleneyat site in the Wadi Gemal area, where the third dive of the day will take place at dusk or at night. Day 7: In the early morning, you will arrive in the Marsa Alam area, on the mythical Elphinstone Reef. You will make 2 dives there, before sailing another two hours to arrive in the early afternoon at the Port Ghalib marina. You can use the platform to rinse your equipment. Your guide will also suggest various extra diving activities to keep you busy on Friday afternoon. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Total Solar Eclipse Expedition - Elphins.programme:
Program
Day 1: Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. A once-in-a-century event, in the middle of the sea On Monday 2 August 2027, the moon's shadow will sweep across Upper Egypt and out over the Red Sea, delivering the second-longest total solar eclipse of the 21st century — and the longest anyone alive today will ever see from this region again. While hundreds of thousands crowd into Luxor, our guests will experience totality from the one place no land observer can reach: the open sea, positioned precisely on the eclipse centerline. For more than six minutes, day becomes night. The temperature drops, stars appear at midday, and the sun's corona blazes above a darkened sea. From the deck you'll watch the moon's shadow race toward you across the water and a 360-degree sunset glow ring the entire horizon — a spectacle only visible from a ship. This is not an eclipse cruise with diving attached. It is a world-class dive safari that happens to sit beneath a once-in-a-century sky. Day 2: First dive - Abu Dabab Second dive - Marsa Alam Reef Day 3: 4 dives: Habili Ali, Gota Al Kabeer, Dangerous Reef Day 4: 3 day dives: Gota Sogyra, Umm Khararem, Paradise + 1 night dive Paradise Day 5: 4 dives: Sataya South, Claudia, Abu Galawa Sagheir Day 6: 4 day dives: Elphinstone, Abu Dabbab Day 7: 2 dives Marsa Shouna Day 8: Check-out from the yacht. Mini Safari Ras Mohamed-Thistlegorm::3.programme:
Program
Day 1: Evening: transfer to New Marina (El Wataneya) Port and embark. Welcome on board, cabin arrangement and boat-briefing. Permission work with port authority, sailing very early next morning. Day 2: Morning: check dive at Temple or Ras Katy. Next dive is Jackfish Alley where you can easily enter the small caves there. The third dive will be the Alternatives, a chain of seven pinnacles with numerous sand patches and resident leopard sharks. Night Diving is very popular here. Day 3: Morning: the boat will sail to the wreck of the Thistlegorm, the most famous of the Red Sea wrecks, maybe even worldwide. There is so much to explore so the plan is a minimum of two dives. The first one is an orientation of the outside and the second dive a penetrating one. For the third dive, your boat will sail to Small Passage where two channels cut the reef system of Sha'ab Mahmoud and connect the sheltered lagoon to the open sea. A night dive inside the lagoon is optional. Day 4: Morning: the first dive of the day will take you to the historical wreck of the Dunraven, which sank in April 1876 - an old wooden wreck with plenty of room for passing through thousands of glassfish that live here in the shade of the wreck. Next dive is Shark and Yolanda Reef, the southernmost tip of the Sinai Peninsula with an endless wall unique in the Red Sea. Sailing back towards Sharm for your third dive at Ras Zatar, Ras Ghozlani or maybe Ras Um Sid. Return to New Marina (El Wataneya) Port and disembark. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons. (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Sinai Classic::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2-7: Morning: sail to nearby Temple or Ras Katy for a check dive. The week-long safari will cover the area from the Strait of Tiran, Ras Mohamed National Park and the Gulf of Suez which is usually visited first. The National Park begins at the small bay of Marsa Ghazlani followed by the larger and deeper bay of Marsa Bareika. Continuing along the coast to Ras Za’atar, Jackfish Alley, Eel Garden, and Shark Observatory, to the southern end of the peninsula with Anemone City, Shark Reef, and Yolanda Reef and ending at the Quay. Because of the geographic position, this is a privileged area distinguished to strong massive currents that transport large quantities of plankton and other food that give rise to an extraordinary growth of stony and soft corals and attract large schools of both reef and pelagic marine fauna, over a thousand species in all. Schooling barracuda, jackfish, tuna and many kinds of sharks swim in these deep blue waters, especially in summer from June to August, sometimes early September. The safari will also take you to famous sites like the wrecks of Dunraven and Thistlegorm, Shag Rock and the wreck of Kingston, sail to Sha’ab Ali where pods of dolphins are common, explore several spots at Sha’ab Mahmouds reef system. Don’t miss the four famous reefs in the Strait of Tiran: Jackson, Thomas, Woodhouse and Gordon Reef, probably the most interesting and richest in marine life. You can choose from several dive sites with superb wall and drift diving. In the afternoon of the 7th day, the boat will return to the Sharm area. Day 7-8: Depending on your check out and flight time return to New Marina (El Wataneya) port and disembark. Transfer to airport or hotel. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

Sinai Wrecks & Reefs::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2-7: Morning: sail to the nearby dive site for a check dive, after into the Gulf of Suez passing Yolanda Reef that is named after a 74 m long Cypriot freighter which struck the reef on the 1st of April 1980. The wreck laid partially submerged on the reef top until a storm caused it to drop. Most of the ship finally has fallen over the drop-off, leaving a huge scar in the slope between Shark and Yolanda Reef. Although, a quantity of the cargo remains for the amusement of the divers: bathtubs, toilets and bathroom fittings. Continue with the historical wrecks of Dunraven. Recovered in the early 1970's, the more than 125 years old wreck is largely intact, totally covered in corals and rich in marine life. The most famous of the Red Sea wrecks maybe even worldwide is the Thistlegorm. The wreck first gained fame when Jacques Cousteau dived it in 1956 but left the actual location a mystery until it was rediscovered in 1992. Lying upright on the seabed at 33 m, the 127 m long and 18 m wide wreck is absolutely impressive. Close to Sha'ab Ali in the early hours of 22 February 1881, the 78 m long Kingston ran aground at the northern edge of the reef that is known as Shag Rock. Crossing the Gulf of Suez will take you to Abu Nuhas, a paradise for wreck lovers which is best known for the abundance of ancient and modern wrecks that lie here: Giannis D, Carnatic, Chrisoula K and Kimon M. All are located on the northern side of the reef, a sandy seafloor at the bottom of a steep sloping coral reef filled with table corals. The reef is very exposed to the prevailing wind and waves and was named after the oldest wreck which was carrying copper (Nuhas in Arabic). If weather permits you can dive the Ulysses or the Rosalie Moller. Only two days after the sinking of the Thistlegorm, the Rosalie Moller was also lying at anchor when hit and went down upright. The location outside of Gubal Island is extremely exposed to the sea, wind, and waves. The dive is deep, bottom time is limited and visibility is lower than elsewhere so this dive is definitely only for very experienced divers. Optional as located far north of Tiran and only reachable with good sea conditions, a rarely dived wreck is the Million Hope. This wreck is one of the youngest in the Egyptian Red Sea and the second largest of the diveable ones. Its size alone makes it a memorable dive. In between wreck dives, you will also visit some outstanding reefs at Sha'ab Mahmoud and Ras Mohammed National Park. Day 7,8: Depending on the guest's check out and flight time, there may be another dive or just snorkeling. Return to New Marina (El Wataneya) Port and disembark. Transfer to airport or hotel. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

The Golden Route (Dahab & More)::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2-6: Depatrure & chck dive. Safari according to the planned route. The Golden Route dive safari truly combines the best of two worlds. Starting and ending in lively Sharm El Sheikh, the route takes you to world-famous dive sites in Ras Mohamed National Park and the Straits of Tiran, and north along the quieter, less-visited “golden coast.” From the impressive Million Hope wreck in Nabq to the pristine reefs near Dahab, and the wreck of the SS Thistlegorm on the other side, this itinerary offers both iconic highlights and peaceful, off-the-beaten-path diving. Aboard comfortable, fast, and stable South Moon 1, we sail along the Sinai coastline, choosing the best dive sites according to conditions. Weather permitting, this safari offers a rich mix of dramatic walls, vibrant coral gardens, iconic dive sites, and the relaxed, almost timeless feeling that makes Dahab truly special. Day 7: 2 dives on the last day. Return to the port. Day 8: Check out from the yacht, and group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons

Elba Reef::11.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, a welcome briefing will be presented by the guide. A check of your diving documents and insurance will be conducted. The captain will then set course for the first dive site, approximately 30 minutes from departure. The 'reorientation' dive briefing will be given by the guide. The second dive will take place in the afternoon. Day 3: On this day, three dives will be offered at the Daedalus site, a potential meeting place with hammerhead sharks. Day 4: You will undertake three dives around the Rocky and Zabargad Islands. The navigation times between the sites vary from 30 to 45 minutes between the islands. The dive sites are carefully selected by your guide based on the weather and the number of boats at the sites. Day 5: For the first day on Elba, you will arrive at the Shaab Kabrit reef to conduct two dives on the Isola Di Levanzo wreck. A third dive will be carried out on the reef. Day 6: Continuing within the Elba Nature Reserve, the captain will take you to Gota Kabrit. After a 1-hour and 30-minute journey, a second dive will be conducted at the Habili Shalal site. Finally, a last dive will be offered at the Ohrob site, a 2- hour and 30-minute navigation away. This program is subject to change based on weather conditions. Day 7: After spending two days on the Elba Reef, you will head north to the Abu Fendira area, near Saint John's. Three dives will be carried out at Abu Fendira. Day 8: In the early morning, the captain and his crew will take you to the Saint John's sites. Three dives will be offered. Navigation times between the sites vary between 30 minutes and 1 hour and 30 minutes in the Saint John's area. Dive sites are carefully selected by your guide based on the weather and the number of boats at the sites. Day 9: We continue our journey northward. On the way, we will stop at Sataya, located in the Fury Shoals area, where you may have the opportunity to swim with dolphins. Three dives will be conducted in the area. Day 10: In the early morning, you will arrive in the Marsa Alam area, at the legendary Elphinstone Reef. You will do 2 dives there before sailing for another two hours to arrive at the Port Ghalib marina in the early afternoon. You can use the rear platform to rinse your equipment. Your guide will also offer various non-diving activities to keep you occupied on Friday afternoon. Day 11: In the morning, you will undertake two dives in the Port Ghalib area, including a search for the green turtles of Shouna. Return to the marina, and you will have the option to stay overnight on the boat on Tuesday evening. Day 12: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure, or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Golden Triangle / BDE::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, your guide will tell you everything you need to know about your program of the week, safety recommendations and, more generally, your life on the boat. Your diving certifications, logbook, and insurance will be checked before leaving the marina. The boat will then sail to the first dive site, 30 minutes away from the marina. Your guide will give you a detailed briefing about your first dive. The second dive will be done in the afternoon. After dinner, the boat will head towards the Brothers Islands for a six hour long trip. This program may be subject to change according to weather conditions and the marina you will depart from. Day 3: Arrived the day before on site, you will do three daytime dives on the stunning drop-offs of the Brothers Islands. Due to new regulations aimed at protecting the marine ecosystem, safari boats are only allowed to spend one day on the Brothers' site. You will then sail all night long to reach Daedalus at the break of dawn. Day 4: Arrived early in the morning, you will do three daytime dives on the amazing drop-off of Daedalus, home of the hammerhead shark. A visit to the lighthouse will be organised by the guide with the authorization of the keepers. Day 5: According to the weather forecast and customers' requests, you will do two or three more dives on Daedalus before sailing towards the coast. It will take about seven hours to reach the site of Abu Dabbab where you will spend the night. According to your time of arrival, a night dive may be organized. Day 6: According to the weather forecast, you will do two or three dives on the stunning drop-offs of Elphinstone. Then the boat will sail back to Abu Dabbab to spend the night in a protected area. If a night dive has not been organized the day before, then we will organize it this day. Day 7: According to the weather forecast and your flight schedules, you will do one or two more dives in the morning. After the last dive, you will have the possibility to rinse all your diving gear on the diving deck at the rear of the boat before sailing for 2 hours to Port Ghalib. This program is based on a departure from Port Ghalib, it can be modified without prior notice by the captain and/or the guide according to the weather conditions. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure, or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

North - Tiran::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After breakfast, your guide will tell you everything you need to know about your programme of the week, safety recommendations and, more generally, your life on the boat. Your diving certifications, logbook and insurance will be checked before leaving the marina. The boat will then sail to the first dive site, 30 minutes away from the marina. Your guide will give you a detailed briefing about your first dive. After lunch you will do your second dive. You will then keep sailing north to reach the El Gouna area where you will spend a quiet and peaceful night moored behind a big reef. Day 3: Arrived the day before on site, you will do your first-two wreck dives in the morning. After lunch you will sail north for two hours before reaching the site where you will do the third dive of the day. Upon request, a night dive may be added. For a quiet and peaceful night, you will spend the night away from the waves, moored behind a big reef. Day 4: At sunrise, the captain and his crew will take you to to the southern tip of the Sinai peninsula where you will dive the wonderful Yolanda Reef in Ras Muhammad National Park. After breakfast, you will sail towards Tiran Island. It takes about two hours from Ras Muhammad to get there. You will be offered the possibility to dive the stunning drop-offs that surround the island. On Jackson reef north, you are likely to encounter many pelagic fishes. You will spend the night behind Tiran Island. Day 5: Early in the morning you will dive on Thomas reef and its outstanding canyon edged by soft corals. After the dive, you will sail for about four hours to reach the mythical wreck of the SS Thistlegorm that you will dive twice. At the end of the day, you will start heading south. You will spend the night in a protected area. Upon request and conditions, a night dive may be added. Day 6: Early in the morning you will do the first dive of the day. After breakfast you will sail for about two hours to reach the Hurghada area. The second dive will take place near Giftun Island, 5km off Hurghada. After lunch you will head south for about four hours to reach the Safaga area. Upon request, a night dive may be added. After dinner the captain and his crew will organise a surprise Egyptian event. Day 7: The last two dives of the week will take place in the Safaga area. The Salem Express shipwreck or three stunning drop- offs will await you to end the week properly. After the last dive, you will have the possibility to rinse all your diving gear on the diving deck at the rear of the boat before sailing for less than an hour to the marina. The estimated time of arrival is 2:00 PM (your guide will tell you all about the leisure activities you can book in the Safaga area to spend an entertaining Friday afternoon). Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure, or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Safaga::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: After a good breakfast, the captain will take you to the first dive site where you will readjust your diving skills, sheltered from the waves and currents. You will then sail to the second site where you will dive from one of our dinghies or from the boat. You will spend the night near Soma Bay. Day 3: The first morning dive will occur on one of the three drop-offs of the Safaga area, at the break of dawn on the south-east side, which increases the possibilities to encounter pelagic fishes hunting for food. The second dive will take place just before lunch on the west side of the drop-off. You will then reach a site called Sha'ab Sheer to dive a beautiful coral garden in 20 meters of water on the western part of the reef, where the sunlight can be enjoyed at that time of the day. Day 4: 30 minutes of navigation at sunrise will be enough to get to the Salem Express, a beautiful shipwreck sunk in the 1990ies. The second dive will take place on the north-east side of Sha'ab Sheer where bottlenose dolphins are often encountered. Your third dive will be a night one! Day 5: It will take only 45 minutes of navigation to reach Panorama Reef, a superb drop-off covered in brown soft coral. With a little bit of luck, you will encounter a turtle on the south-east part of the reef. You will then sail for half an hour to reach Middle Reef where you will dive for the third time of the day on the western side. Day 6: At the break of dawn, you will hop into a dinghy to go to the northern part of the reef where you will discover a fantastic plateau and huge gorgonian sea-fans. Just before lunch you will visit the eastern side of the reef that hosts one of the most beautiful gardens of hard corals in the Red Sea. You will then have a 45 minute navigation towards Tobia Arbaa where you will enjoy night-diving with lion fish. Day 7: After breakfast you will discover a site called Gamul Soraya where schools of snappers and garden eels await you. The second dive, in the afternoon, will take place on Tobia Kebir where beautiful eagle rays are encountered on a regular basis. You will then go back to the marina. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure, or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Best of Dahab and Tiran::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Arrival and Embarkation (Hurghada) Guests are greeted at the Hurghada airport and transferred to the liveaboard. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome drink and a refreshing towel, followed by an introduction to the crew and a safety briefing. Guests settle into their cabins, followed by equipment checks with assistance from the dive team. Spend the evening relaxing, enjoying a delicious dinner onboard, and getting ready for the adventure ahead. Days 2 to 5: Diving Dahab and Tiran Over these four days, guests will explore the underwater treasures of Dahab and Tiran. Dive highlights may include: Dahab's Blue Hole: A world-famous dive site with dramatic walls and a deep, azure blue drop-off. Canyon Reef: Known for its mesmerizing caverns and swim-throughs, teeming with marine life. Tiran's Jackson Reef: A spectacular site for spotting schooling fish, reef sharks, and vibrant coral gardens. Woodhouse Reef: A thrilling drift dive with sweeping currents and potential sightings of eagle rays and turtles. Each day offers 2–3 dives, with opportunities for night dives on select evenings. The dive schedule is complemented by periods of relaxation, snorkeling, and enjoying the stunning views of the Red Sea. Day 6: Return to Hurghada After breakfast, the liveaboard makes its way back to Hurghada. The last two dives may be scheduled for today, or it may be a non-diving day, allowing guests time to clean and pack their equipment. Guests can relax on deck, swap dive stories, or explore Hurghada on their own before a farewell dinner onboard. Day 7: Disembarkation (Hurghada) Guests bid farewell to the crew and disembark. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Best of Tiran::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Days 2-6: Departing & check dive. Cruising according to the planned route. Day 7: 2 dives on the last day. Return to the port. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. The best sites in the area of Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, Gubal Strait and the Strait of Tiran in the Gulf of Aqaba. (As with all circuits, order and site selection can not only be contractual; they can be varied due to the weather and/or state of the sea). A circuit that will take you to the Strait of Tiran, through the reserve of Ras Mohamed and wrecks like the mythical Thistlegorm, Rosalie Moeller... This tour will allow you to dive on steep drop-offs, reefs with fish, pelagic carangos, eagle rays, sharks... Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Brother Islands - Daedalus - Elphinstone.programme:
Program
Day 1: Check-in from 4:00 PM. Overnight on the boat. Day 2: 1st dive - Ras Disha. 2nd dive - Wreck of the Salem Express. 3rd dive - Middle Reef. Day 3: 1st dive - Big Brother South. 2nd dive - Big Brother (Numidia wreck). 3rd dive - Little Brother. Day 4: 1st dive - Daedalus North. 2nd dive - Daedalus East. 3rd dive - Daedalus South. Day 5: 1st dive - Daedalus. 2nd dive - Daedalus. 3rd dive - Daedalus West. Day 6: 1st Dive - Elphinstone North. 2nd dive - Elphinstone South. 3rd Dive - Marsa Alam Area. 4th dive - night dive. Day 7: 1st dive - Panorama Reef. 2nd dive - El Mina wreck. Day 8: Check-out from 9:00 am. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Daedalus - Rocky - Zabargad - Elphinston.programme:
Program
Day 1: Check-in day. Guests can check in from 5 pm until 3 am the following morning to get to the boat in time. Services start on day 1 after check-in, and evening dinner is included on board. The boat leaves between 9 and 10 am on day 2. Day 2: Departure for St. John’s after breakfast. Days 3–6: Up to 3 dives a day exploring the stunning reefs. Day 7: Dives are planned, but this depends on the flight schedule of the guests. The boat will be back in the afternoon. The last night will be spent at the marina, and dinner will be served on board. Day 8: Breakfast is included, and check-out is between 8 and 9 am. Guests can go straight to the airport to catch their flight. Transfers are organized by the boat. Rocky Island and Zabargad Rocky Island has become a shelter and nesting place for a large variety of birds. Zabargad, the bigger of the two islands, has quite a steep relief and is surrounded by a marvelous turquoise lagoon. During summer, it becomes a rendezvous place for turtles, where they gather to lay their eggs. The best description would be: wild landscapes and isolated sites, lost in the middle of the Red Sea. Daedalus On the northern side of Daedalus, we will make a sunrise dive. This is the most exposed side of Daedalus, with strong sea currents and the best chance of encounters with pelagic species. It is quite common to dive with schools of more than 20 hammerhead sharks. Carangidae and tunas are regularly present. We will then leave the deep zone to explore the reef wall. This exploration requires close attention, as the wall is full of holes and overhangs. Many black coral branches can be seen colonizing the reef. While ascending, don’t forget to look up: you may see barracudas nearby. Zabargad On Zabargad Island, you can still see fragments of emerald-like rocks that gave the island its fame and name. Zabargad is the Arabic name for the green-olive mineral that once filled this semi-volcanic island. The dive site is characterized by peaks, canyons, caves, and walls. You can encounter tunas, scorpionfish, leopard sharks, nurse sharks, angelfish, groupers, morays, blue dotted stingrays, and mantas. Rocky Five km south of Zabargad lies Rocky Island, near the Sudanese border. Undoubtedly, Rocky Island is one of the wildest diving sites in Egypt. Diving over the shallow platform, which shelters all kinds of marine life, leads to a wall covered with giant gorgonians, sponges, and corals. The south of the island is a meeting point for whitefin sharks, grey reef sharks, and mantas. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)

Fury Shoal::7.programme:
Program
Day 1: Meet & greet at the airport. Group transfer to the port. Onboarding, meeting the crew & briefing. Day 2: Departure in the morning around 8-9 am, 2 check dives near the coast of Marsa Alam, 3rd dive or possible night dive in the area, sailing overnight to the Fury Shoal reefs. Days 3-5: Spending time at Fury's, 3-4 dives possible per day, including 1 possible night dive. Possible dive sites: Malahi, Shab Claudio, Shab Maksur, Sataya/Dolphin Reef. Day 6: Return to Port Ghalib, possibly 2 dives in Elphinstone or in the Marsa Alam area – weather dependent. Day 7: The last 2 dives in the Marsa Alam area, the last night on board. Day 8: Check-out from the yacht, group transfer to the airport. Routes can be affected by adverse weather conditions and unforeseen events, force majeure or other similar reasons (Please note that night dives are not allowed in Marine Parks)
